content: Rectified spirit, also known as rectified alcohol, is a highly concentrated form of alcohol that has undergone purification through a process called rectification, which involves repeated distillation. This type of alcohol is utilized for various purposes, including medicinal applications, as a household solvent, and as an ingredient in mixed alcoholic beverages. Neutral grain spirits, a subset of rectified spirits, are specifically derived from grains. However, rectified spirits can also be produced from other plant-based materials, with sugar beets and potatoes being common sources. In certain countries, such as India, the use of rectified spirits for nonmedical purposes is prohibited, whereas in most industrialized nations, their use is permitted. In Canada, rectified spirits were banned until recent years. In the United States, a rectified spirit known as Spirytus Stawski is imported from Poland by Stawski Imports, based in Chicago, Illinois. This product contains 96% alcohol by volume (192 proof) and is also available in a 76% alcohol (152 proof) variant. It is a colorless, tasteless, and nearly odorless liquid. Another widely recognized rectified spirit in the United States is Everclear, which is produced by Luxco. Everclear is available in two strengths: 95% alcohol (190 proof) and 75.5% alcohol (151 proof). However, the 190-proof version is banned in certain states. In Poland, rectified spirit is referred to as spirytus rektyfikowany. The Polish version is distilled to a concentration slightly above 95% alcohol by volume (190 proof). While tourists in Poland are allowed to purchase and consume spirytus, exporting it is prohibited by law. Despite this restriction, enforcement of the export ban is relatively lenient. In Germany, rectified spirit is commonly referred to as Primasprit in colloquial terms or Naturalalkohol in more technical language. It is available in Germany at a concentration of 96.5% alcohol by volume (193 proof). In this country, Primasprit is predominantly used for the preparation of homemade liqueurs, with other applications being relatively uncommon. Most of the Primasprit produced in Germany is derived from grains, making it a type of neutral grain spirit.
